title: One Bowl Is $3, One Is $300 — Same Pattern, Which Is Real? | China Travel Expert
description:
Two bowls, the same blue pattern. One costs a few dollars, one costs hundreds. Can you tell which is real?

The cheap bowl is machine-printed — the pattern is a transfer, applied fast. The expensive one is hand-painted in Jingdezhen, China's porcelain capital for roughly a thousand years. Traditional Jingdezhen porcelain runs through 70-plus hand steps, and one bad moment in the kiln can ruin a whole batch — which is why genuine hand-thrown, hand-painted pieces start near $150 and climb into the hundreds, while a printed bowl is a few dollars.

🧭 Expert Tip: flip a piece over and look at the base and the brush lines — real hand-painting never repeats exactly, and the foot ring shows tool marks a machine can't fake.
